chapter: The band, its players and singers
title: Working with Tony Bennett, Sinatra and other singers; never 'the best'
summary: Basie denies saying Tony Bennett had the best pipes, insisting he never calls anyone the best, and praises Sinatra, Joe Williams and above all Jimmy Rushing.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Okay, what was it like in Vegas when
you were -- hey, you were accompanying Tony Bennett, weren't you, in Las Vegas.
Yes.
What was that about?
Great, it was always great. We worked with Tony quite often, very often. He's nice to work with.
I seem to recall you once saying that you thought he had the best pipes in the business.
I have never said that about anybody, don't you ever quote me as saying anything like that. 'I thought he had the best pipes,' I didn't say that.
Okay.
I can't ever say --
I won't quote you _ I don't go out and quote you. I am facing you with it.
I never told you that either.
Then contradict me. I am saying it to you, not to anyone out there, right.

I will always say -- I always say that somebody is one of the best. I never say anybody who is the best of anything. I mean like -- I would say to me, who is the best piano, the best one, who is this guy saying who is the best. And just remember now how can I say that, and I worked with Ella, I worked with Billy Eckstine, I worked with Frank Sinatra, I worked with Joe Williams on and off, the
best, that's a hell of a thing for me to say with me when he's working with all these people and Sarah, and all these people. How can I say that.
I guess you didn't then.
You are damn right I didn't.
Okay.
And Tony and I were great, like we're on one hand.
Yeah.

Yeah, and still -- chairman of the board, and he -- Frank's my man. We're real buddies, you know him, and we're tight and have a ball each time, because I mean that's really one of the ideas why we were work together, we really have a ball, have fun. Frank sings happy when he wants to, you know what I mean, and he's a happy singer.
And he knows where it is and fits in as a swing singer. Jimmy, Joe Williams. My main man is little Jimmy Rushing, he started and you know where he stood.
